listBibl.bibl: Felix Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, vol. 1 (Halle: Niemeyer, 1903), p. 416

A semi-literal English rendering of the Latin text, created for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model made by Anthropic. It is a crib to help the reader with the Latin, and should not be treated as a separate translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: Iud Dei IX 3.3
div.ab: Scímus igitur et fideliter confitemur, té omnia in principio creásse, creata uero benedixisse et benedicta nutibus humanis subdidisse,
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 416 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: We know therefore and faithfully confess that in the beginning you created all things, and blessed what was created, and subjected what was blessed to the command of men,
